content.body:
The Douglas-built Havoc I was a very effective intruder aircraft. This sturdy and high-performance airframe continued to evolve through the war as the A-20, and eventually into the A-26 Invader, perhaps the ultimate expression of the intruder-style bomber as it evolved during the war years.
Used by France, Britain, Russia, and the USAAF in almost every theater of war during the 1940s, the A-20 was truly a legendary attack aircraft. While the early models such as the ones in Battleground Europe at present were only armed with four pilot controlled rifle caliber machineguns and one defensive dorsal gunner, later on, these would wind up being multiple (up to 8 or 10) .50 caliber heavy machineguns or four 20 mm cannons.
British Havoc I's were the first aircraft used by USAAF aircrews against German targets in WWII during the early famous low altitude "rodeo" raids staged against airfield targets in then German-held French coastal territory.
CREW POSITIONS: 1 Pilot 2 Bombardier 3 Tail Gunner
